history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a SIKH GURDWARA, not a Hindu temple: place listings categorize it as a 'Sikh Temple' (gurdwara), and the congregation runs it as a sangat place of worship under the Guru Granth Sahib, with no Hindu murti worship. The referent is the Gurdwara Singh Sabha on Handiaya Bazar Road / Gurudwara Street, Sadar Bazar (near Old Tehsil Road), Barnala, also listed as Gurudwara Singh Sabha Dashmesh Nagar and 'Gurdwara Shri Guru Singh Sabha Sadar Bazar Barnala' (the latter from a YouTube video title of its kirtan). Several other Singh Sabha gurdwaras exist in nearby villages (Tapa, Nim Wala Maur, Dashmesh Nagar), so the Sadar Bazar one is the town referent. No founding history or verifiable historical facts are published online. No reliable image of this specific gurdwara was found, so media is intentionally empty. Correction note: district is Barnala (Barnala became a separate district in 2006).

name: Gurdwara Singh Sabha
town_description: Barnala is the headquarters of Barnala district, Punjab (a separate district since 2006, carved out of Sangrur). It sits at about 227 m elevation on the plains of Malwa, connected by rail and road to Bathinda, Ludhiana, Sangrur and Mansa.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport, about 150 km away (verify).
travel.road: Handiaya Bazar Road / Sadar Bazar area in central Barnala town; reachable by road within the town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Gurpurabs and Vaisakhi for festive visits.
